children: is stepping up efforts to increase its value proposition among consumers and align with franchisees on a longer-term approach designed to strengthen its competitive position against fast-food rivals, specifically Burger King

According to a message seen by Bloomberg, the company sees “compelling value as critical to bringing customers through our doors and strengthening the baseline” of McDonald’s business. The plans are being developed by McDonald’s
management as well as a group of franchisees.
However, a more affordable menu and cooperation from franchisees might not be enough to reverse sluggish sales in the short term.

“We think it will be a tall task to sell investors that McDonald’s has the right recipe for U.S. same-store sales over the next twelve months,” Citi Research analyst Jon Tower wrote in a note to clients on Thursday, adding that getting franchisees on board with value offerings has been a tough sell for the hamburger chain.

At the company’s Investor Day on September 23, Tower expects to hear the company’s plan for value offerings, beverage, chicken, and GLP-1 resilience, although timelines and the costs of initiatives will be crucial to the turnaround efforts.

But the event will also give the company an opportunity to make it clear to franchisees that adherence to pricing recommendations will be a key factor in evaluating franchise renewals. Although the company sets menu options and pricing, franchisees have the option to set their own prices, an outcome that negatively impacted the parent company’s results. Last quarter, sales at established McDonald’s restaurants increased by just 0.8%, their slowest pace of growth since the first quarter of 2025.

Tower lowered his EPS estimates for 2026 and 2027 by $0.03 and $0.02 to $12.84 and $14.26, respectively, and cut his price target by 10% to $3.10 to reflect a lower market multiple and expectation for continued same-store sales softness.

title: Can McDonald's turn its value strategy into a turnaround?
